**Chinese name:** 豪威集成电路（集团）股份有限公司 (Háowēi Jíchéng Diànlù (Jítuán) Gǔfèn Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
OmniVision Technologies (originally a US company) was acquired by a Chinese consortium led by Will Semiconductor in 2019; the parent formally renamed itself from Will Semiconductor (韦尔股份) to OmniVision Group (豪威集团/豪威集成电路（集团）股份有限公司) and completed its Hong Kong listing in mid-January 2026 (first day +16.2%, market cap >HK$152.9bn) — a notable case of a Chinese fabless firm acquiring a once-independent Western chip brand outright rather than building one from scratch. Unlike most other entries updated in this tracker's 2026 sweep, OmniVision's recent results moved the other direction: Q1 2026 net profit fell 41.9% YoY to ¥503 million, and H1 2026 revenue was essentially flat at ¥14.03 billion with net profit down 39.9% to ¥1.22 billion (CIS -10.5% on smartphone softness and storage-cost crowding-out; analog +17.1%, display +12.9%, 'emerging' machine-vision/robotics CIS +47.1% and +71.2% respectively) — a useful reminder that China's chip sector is not uniformly booming even where AI/memory-linked names are. Management then did something unusual for an A-share name and pre-disclosed Q3 operating data (25 August): Q3 revenue ¥7.58–8.13 billion, i.e. between -3.2% and +3.9% YoY, with gross margin recovering sequentially to 29.4–30.7% — stabilization guidance rather than a new spiral. 2025 full-year net profit had been reported up ~498% YoY to ¥3.3 billion, making the 2026 decline a reversal from an unusually strong prior-year base.
:::

## What does this firm design?

CMOS image sensors (smartphone and automotive cameras), plus analog and display driver solutions.
